currentContext.business: Polyspin Exports Limited manufactures FIBC (Flexible Intermediate Bulk Container) bags and PP woven bags, along with PP woven fabrics and multifilament yarn, from three units at Cholapuram South near Rajapalayam, Virudhunagar District, Tamil Nadu; Unit-I is a 100% EOU housing the FIBC Bags and Woven Bags Division. FIBC is described by the Company as an integral part of the global industrial packaging segment serving chemicals, agriculture, food processing, pharmaceuticals and construction end-users, and the business is export-oriented with India's presence concentrated in the United States and Europe. Multifilament yarn is largely made for internal use - of 7,56,175 Kgs produced during FY26, 7,55,180 Kgs were captively consumed for FIBC bag production - and the Textile Division was discontinued with its assets fully disposed of in the second quarter of FY 2024-25.

currentContext.expansion: The only expansion activity described is modernisation rather than greenfield capacity addition: during FY26 the Company installed six Nova 62 circular looms at a cost of Rs.1.22 Crore, replacing six old looms, stated to be in order to increase production. On the energy side the Company's 1.304 MW (1304 kWp) rooftop solar plant was in operation during the year, with its output used for captive consumption. No new plant, line or site, no commissioning or ramp-up timeline, and no forward capex programme is disclosed in this bundle; the outlook language on higher capacity utilisation is written about the FIBC industry generally, not about a company project.

The only pipeline reference is industry-level: following the moderation of US tariff rates late in the year, the report notes 'Improvement in order flows and customer sentiment.'

risks.note: Raw-material price volatility, 'particularly polypropylene', is listed first among the industry's Risks and Concerns and is cited as one of the two factors that moderated capacity utilisation levels in certain periods during the year. The Board's risk table separately flags that unavailability of raw material can diminish production capacity, mitigated only by long-term relationships with PP granule suppliers.

The business and the Indian FIBC industry are export-oriented, which the report says exposes them to global demand cycles and leaves them 'exposed to external demand conditions'. Unit-I is a 100% EOU and the industry's presence is concentrated in the United States and Europe, so the revenue base is geographically concentrated.

During the year the imposition of higher US tariffs on FIBC imports reduced price competitiveness in the US market, caused a temporary slowdown in export volumes and put pressure on margins for export-oriented players. Tariff rates moderated later in the year, but 'Changes in trade policies and tariff structures' remains a standing risk and uncertainty in global trade policy is named as a driver of lower capacity utilisation.

The Board's risk-management table names Industry Risk as 'Softening demand for FIBC bags will impact offtake', with a Long Term outlook; the stated mitigation is to minimise cost of production and build long-term relationships to become the supplier of choice.

risks.risk: Competition from other low-cost manufacturing countries
risks.note: Listed in Risks and Concerns as competitive pressure on the Indian FIBC industry, whose position rests on cost competitiveness and pricing/quality parity; the report also notes that global sourcing shifts currently favour India, making the advantage contingent on relative cost.

'Increasing regulatory and environmental compliance requirements' is listed in Risks and Concerns, and the Board's risk table adds Regulatory Risk - a change in regulation or legislation may derail production strategy - mitigated by consistently tracking regulations and statutory industry compliances.

The statutory auditor's Key Audit Matter for both the standalone and consolidated financial statements is the evaluation of uncertain tax positions: the Company / Group 'has material uncertain tax positions including matters under dispute which involves significant judgement to determine the possible outcome of these disputes' (Note 33.3 standalone, Note 35.1(ii) consolidated).

risks.risk: Unconfirmed balances of trade debtors and creditors
risks.note: The auditor carries an Emphasis of Matter in both the standalone and consolidated reports drawing attention to the status of confirmation of balances of Trade Debtors, Trade Creditors and other parties (Note 33.8 standalone, Note 35.6 consolidated); the opinion is not modified in respect of these matters.
